title: Marsden Medal 2026: early career research on endocranial anatomy, species boundaries, ancient DNA, and more
content: The Linnean Society of London has regularly awarded an annual prize medal in memory of former Executive Secretary Dr John C. Marsden. The awarded medal honours the best published research paper resulting from a student PhD thesis, and the Medals and Awards Committee recently voted to align this prize exclusively with content from its portfolio of journals. Nominated papers are assessed across four judging criteria: (i) an overall evaluation of the work; (ii) originality and novelty; (iii) readability and organization; and (iv) presentation. I am thrilled that papers published in Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society are eligible for this award. Our community of authors includes many early career researchers, and we are proud to facilitate experiences with peer review and constructive scientific discourse. Celebrating their work with this annual prize is a valuable addition to what we can offer potential authors and will allow us to contribute more directly to the professional development of zoologists. The direct link between the John C. Marsden Medal and Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society also provides new avenues for the Linnean Society to promote the work of our authors through blogs, online lectures, and in-person events at the historic Burlington House located in central London.
